learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how the world's largest democracy votes! Learn the difference between election systems and how the Election Commission ensures fairness.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: सर्वाधिक वोट पाने वाले की जीत

main_concepts.simple_explanation: In this system, the country is divided into small constituencies. The candidate who gets the highest number of votes in a constituency wins. They don't need a 50% majority, just more votes than anyone else. India uses this for Lok Sabha.

A party gets seats in the legislature exactly in proportion to the percentage of votes it gets overall. India uses a complex version of PR for the election of the President, Vice President, and Rajya Sabha.
FPTP is simple for common voters to understand. It offers a clear choice between specific candidates (not just parties) and usually gives a clear majority to one party, ensuring a stable government.

To ensure fair representation for historically oppressed groups (SCs and STs), certain constituencies are reserved. Only candidates from these communities can stand for election there, but all voters in that area vote.
An independent, constitutional body that conducts free and fair elections in India. It prepares voter lists, recognizes parties, allots symbols, and enforces the Model Code of Conduct.

fun_activity.title: 🗳️ Class Election Simulation
fun_activity.instructions: Hold a vote for a class monitor using FPTP. If Candidate A gets 40%, B gets 35%, and C gets 25%, A wins. Notice that A won even though 60% of the class did NOT vote for them! That's FPTP.

exam_tips: 📌 Prepare a clear comparison table between the FPTP and PR systems.
📌 Know why separate electorates (British era) were rejected in favor of reserved constituencies.
📌 Highlight the independence of the Election Commission (e.g., security of tenure for the Chief Election Commissioner).
quick_recap: ⭐ India has Universal Adult Franchise: every citizen aged 18 and above can vote.
⭐ The Delimitation Commission works with the Election Commission to draw the boundaries of constituencies.
⭐ The FPTP system often gives the winning party more seats than their vote share percentage.
